page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 20 vCPUs and 20 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model under the KVM hypervisor. The system features 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.8 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, it integrates three NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, delivering a combined total of 144 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this configuration, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 3088.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 4190.38, both placing in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% with a Geekbench multi-core score of 17663.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 62711.03. Memory performance is also robust, showing a read-only large block bandwidth of 306.94 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 144.32 GB/sec. Text processing and compression tasks also rank in the top 10%, while ray tracing and encryption benchmarks perform at average levels.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers a high-density GPU configuration relative to its 20 vCPUs, making it highly efficient for workloads that require heavy parallel processing without needing a massive CPU core count. However, the shared CPU allocation model and the complete lack of local storage represent key architectural tradeoffs that require external storage solutions. This configuration is highly suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as machine learning training, data science pipelines, rendering, and high-throughput database operations.
